title: Practice 5: Running, swimming, climbing, crawling, dragging

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Вы когда-нибудь ___ (кататься — to roll (oneself)) на гидроцикле?
exercises.why: **катались** is the past tense (plural) of **кататься** (to ride in a vehicle) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **катиться** for one direction. past: он ката́лся · она ката́лась · оно ката́лось · они ката́лись. — Wiktionary, «кататься» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Мне нравится кататься на лыжах, на коньках, на велосипеде и на лодке. — I like to ski, skate, cycle, and row.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Have you ever ridden a jet ski?
exercises.context: Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Ты когда-нибудь ___ (кататься — to roll (oneself)) на гидроцикле?
exercises.why: **катался** is the past tense (masculine) of **кататься** (to ride in a vehicle) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **катиться** for one direction. past: он ката́лся · она ката́лась · оно ката́лось · они ката́лись. — Wiktionary, «кататься» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Мне нравится кататься на лыжах, на коньках, на велосипеде и на лодке. — I like to ski, skate, cycle, and row.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Have you ever ridden a jet ski?
exercises.context: Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Мы пустили своих жуков ___ (бежать — to run, one way) наперегонки.
exercises.why: **бежать** (the infinitive) ((imperfective only) to run, to be running) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **бегать** for many directions. — Wiktionary, «бежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs бегать-бежать, побежать belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить-идти, пойти. Note that in the conjugation of the verb "бежать", the consonants "ж" and "г" are alternated: я бегу, ты бежишь, они бегут. Note also that in all persons, except the 3rd person plural, it belongs to the 2nd conjugation: ты бежишь, он бежит, мы бежим, вы бежите. In the 3rd person plural it belongs to the 1st conjugation: они бегут.» — DLI, Lesson 82.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Как быстро ты ___ (бегать — to run, there and back or in general)!
exercises.why: **бегаешь** is the present tense (2nd person singular) of **бегать** (to run) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **бежать** for one direction. present: я бе́гаю · ты бе́гаешь · он бе́гает · мы бе́гаем · вы бе́гаете · они бе́гают. — Wiktionary, «бегать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs бегать-бежать, побежать belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить-идти, пойти.» — DLI, Lesson 82.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Хорошая кожа будет ___ (носиться — to carry on foot (oneself)) годы.
exercises.why: **носиться** (the infinitive) (to rush, to rush around, to run/drive around (on a high speed)) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **нестись** for one direction. — Wiktionary, «носиться» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Почему собаки ___ (гоняться — to drive, chase (oneself)) за белками?
exercises.why: **гоняются** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **гоняться** (to chase, to pursue [with за (za) ‘someone’]) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **гнаться** for one direction. present: я гоня́юсь · ты гоня́ешься · он гоня́ется · мы гоня́емся · вы гоня́етесь · они гоня́ются. — Wiktionary, «гоняться» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: The Ice Age was a time when woolly mammoths roamed the Earth.
exercises.why: **бродили** is the past tense (plural) of **бродить** (to wander, to roam, to ramble) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **брести** for one direction. past: он броди́л · она броди́ла · оно броди́ло · они броди́ли. — Wiktionary, «бродить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite).» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «по Земле» — movement in various directions, not towards one goal.  The other choice: **брели** is from **брести**, the one-direction verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.ru: Ледниковый период был временем, когда по Земле ___ волосатые мамонты.

(Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: По озеру ___ (плыть — to swim, float, sail, one way) маленькая лодочка.
exercises.why: **плыла** is the past tense (feminine) of **плыть** (to swim, to float) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **плавать** for many directions. past: он плы́л · она плыла́ · оно плы́ло, плыло́ · они плы́ли. — Wiktionary, «плыть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verb плавать — плыть, поплыть belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить — идти, пойти; "плавать" (like "ходить") is a "repeated function" verb. Note the ways in which it is used: Я умею плавать. — I know how to swim. Дерево плавает в воде. — Wood floats in water. Я плаваю на этом корабле. — I sail (work) on this ship. In naval terminology the verb "идти" instead of "плыть" is commonly used: Я иду на этом корабле. Наш корабль идёт по Чёрному морю. Мы шли в Архангельск.» — DLI, Lesson 73.  Compare: «Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.» (Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Across the lake sailed a little boat.
exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

The other choice: **таскает** is from **таскать**, the many-directions verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Белки очень хорошо ___ (лазать — to climb, there and back or in general).
exercises.why: **лазают** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **лазать** (to climb, to clamber) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **лезть** for one direction. present: я ла́заю · ты ла́заешь · он ла́зает · мы ла́заем · вы ла́заете · они ла́зают. — Wiktionary, «лазать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite).» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
